result.title: Scaling Laws for Vision-Language Fusion
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as central foundation models combining multimodal perception with text comprehension. While VLMs are traditionally built via late fusion by continued pre-training an off-the-shelf language model on multimodal (image-text) data, mixing modalities from the start of pre-training (early fusion) has recently gained traction. However, the fundamental trade-offs between these paradigms remain poorly understood, resulting in expensive and heuristic-driven training recipes. In this paper, we systematically analyze the learning dynamics of these multimodal pre-training processes, showing that validation losses during vision-language fusion can be modeled by separating the base learning trajectory, where different data types contribute at distinct rates, from a distribution shift driven by the competition between modalities. We derive a scaling law that unifiedly describes these dynamics, enabling accurate loss predictions across mixture ratios, training steps, and model sizes. Crucially, our law characterizes the trade-off between early and late fusion: under a fixed data budget, early fusion preserves text performance while late fusion favors vision performance, yielding a trade-off that increasingly tilts toward early fusion as model size scales. Extensive experiments confirm that our scaling law reliably captures multimodal learning dynamics and governs fusion decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文系统分析视觉-语言预训练的学习动力学，将验证损失拆分为基础学习轨迹（不同数据类型以不同速率贡献）与模态竞争引起的分布偏移，并据此导出统一的 scaling law，用于预测不同混合比例、训练步数和模型规模下的损失，刻画 early fusion 与 late fusion 的权衡。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「基础轨迹＋模态竞争偏移」的损失分解与预测框架可供核查是否能用于建模 VLM 训练中视觉与文本贡献的分配及预算取舍，但论文不涉及 latent 推理状态生成与使用，与 LVR 主线联系较外围。
